title: Dedicated capacity modular SKUs + security questionnaire readiness
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a modular SKU and pricing experiment framework for Dedicated capacity that supports: reserved GPU commitments, burst credits for short-term spikes, configurable autoscaling policies, and clear SLA tiers. Deliverables include a pricing matrix, experiment plan for A/B testing pricing shapes, contract appendix language for SLAs and performance credits, and completed baseline answers for common enterprise security questionnaires (SOC2/SaaS vendor, ISO, and custom RFPs).
acceptance_criteria: Pricing matrix with at least 3 modular SKUs (Reserved-Minimum, Reserved-Standard, Reserved-High) published in Confluence
Two pricing experiment cohorts defined with hypothesis, sample size, and target uplift metrics (conversion, ARR per customer)
Draft contract appendix with SLA definitions and performance credit formulas reviewed by Legal
SQ cheat-sheet (one-pager) completed with KMS/HSM, audit logs, data residency, and pen-test cadence answers and validated by Security
UI/Console dropdowns and billing API changes scoped and a GitHub PR opened for required backend telemetry
Operational runbook for burst-credit accounting and autoscaler behavior documented and linked to on-call playbook
experiment_plan: Hypothesis A: Lower upfront committed price + smaller burst pool will increase initial committed customers by >= 10% vs baseline
Hypothesis B: Higher committed price with larger burst credits reduces churn for high-traffic customers by 15% over 6 months
Cohort selection: New signups hitting the Dedicated onboarding flow, randomized at org-level, exclude enterprise contract leads
Primary metrics: committed conversion rate, ARR per org at 90 days, effective cost-per-served-token estimate, support ticket rate related to capacity
Secondary metrics: average burst credit utilization, autoscaler-triggered failovers, SLO breach count
Duration: 12-week experiment window with 4-week ramp and 8-week observation
Success criteria: statistically significant lift on conversion or churn reduction and unit economics within target thresholds
pricing_matrix_proposal: Reserved-Minimum: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, baseline throughput, 10% burst credits (time-limited), monthly commit, price = $X per GPU-hour
Reserved-Standard: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, higher throughput, 25% burst credits, 6-12 month commit discount, price = $Y per GPU-hour
Reserved-High: customer-managed node sizes, premium autoscale buffers, 50% burst credits, custom contract, price = negotiated tier
Autoscale add-on: per-minute billing for transient nodes beyond reserved capacity, capped burst pool and soft vs hard limits configurable
Burst credits: measured in GPU-minutes, accrue monthly, expire after billing period; accounting rules documented

SLA tiers: Bronze (99.5% uptime, best-effort latency), Silver (99.9% uptime, 95th perc latency target), Gold (99.95% uptime, 99th perc latency target) with clearly defined remediation and credit calculation
contract_and_sq_tasks: Work with Legal to add a dedicated appendix: SLA definitions, performance credit calculation, maintenance windows and notification windows
Prepare a 1-page SQ cheat-sheet answering vendor RFP common questions: data flow diagram, encryption in transit/rest, KMS/HSM integrations, key custody options
Collect artifacts: SOC2 report stub, pen-test summary (last 12 months), list of third-party subprocessors
Assign Security to validate answers and escalate any items requiring product changes (e.g., redaction support, dedicated logging endpoints)
Draft sample contract language for burst credits billing and dispute resolution for SLO breaches
Coordinate with Sales Ops to ensure pricing is represented in CPQ templates and marketplace SKUs
